finding.claim: _validate_sub returns without checking the caller-supplied subject when the token has no sub claim, so decode(..., subject=X) accepts signed tokens lacking sub (fail-open; iss and aud fail closed).
finding.source: Token payload lacking a 'sub' claim, signed by the same key/issuer (e.g. a different token type sharing the key).
finding.sink: Caller's subject-based authorization check via decode(..., subject=...).

trace.note: decode() forwards subject to decode_complete
decode_complete passes subject into _validate_claims
_validate_sub(payload, subject) is called when verify_sub is set
'if "sub" not in payload: return' exits before comparing to subject

finding.guards_checked: Signature verified first (api_jws.py:269-277). Present sub must be a string and must equal subject (api_jwt.py:449-454). Sibling checks fail closed: missing aud raises (api_jwt.py:529-532), missing iss raises (api_jwt.py:571-572). Verified by reading only; not executed.

finding.claim: With cache_keys=True, get_signing_key is wrapped in an LRU cache with no time expiry, so a signing key removed from the JWKS (rotation or compromise) keeps verifying until evicted by other kids.
finding.source: A signing key that the IdP has removed from its JWKS; the attacker holds a token signed with it.
finding.sink: Signature acceptance using the cached PyJWK key (api_jws.py:416-417).

trace.note: cache_keys enables lru_cache(maxsize=max_cached_keys) on get_signing_key
self.get_signing_key replaced by cached wrapper
docstring documents no time-based expiration for this tier
alg_obj.verify runs with the cached key and succeeds

finding.guards_checked: Only successful lookups are cached. The 5-minute JWKS lifespan (jwks_client.py:92-96) does not apply to this tier. Behaviour is documented, but there is no revocation or max-age path. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: PyJWKClient accepts any http/https URI and follows redirects with urlopen, forwarding configured headers (e.g. Authorization). If the application builds the URI from token data (jku), an attacker can host a JWKS or reach internal hosts (SSRF).
finding.source: Attacker-influenced JWKS URI (e.g. a jku header value), or a redirect from the JWKS endpoint.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP request in fetch_data and trust of the returned key set.

trace.note: urlparse scheme check only; accepts any http/https host
urllib Request built with self.headers
urlopen follows redirects; scheme guard applies only to the initial URI
attacker-served JSON parsed with json.load and no size limit, then cached

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (http/https) only. No host allowlist, no private-address block, no redirect cap, no response size limit. Severity medium if the application derives the URI from token data; low otherwise. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: Every unknown kid in an unauthenticated token triggers a synchronous, unthrottled JWKS refetch, enabling outbound request amplification and thread exhaustion (DoS).
finding.source: Unauthenticated token with a random kid, read from the unverified header.
finding.sink: Outbound HTTP GET to the JWKS endpoint (30 s default timeout).

trace.note: get_signing_key_from_jwt reads kid from the unverified header
get_signing_key calls get_signing_keys() (cached)
on miss, get_signing_keys(refresh=True) is called
get_jwk_set calls fetch_data when refresh bypasses cache

finding.guards_checked: None rate-limits refresh or enforces a minimum refresh interval. Failed lookups are not cached, so each request causes another fetch. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: The signature segment is decoded with a lenient base64 decoder that ignores non-alphabet characters and unused trailing bits, so one valid signature has several token-string encodings. Token-string identity (replay caches, denylists) can be bypassed. ECDSA also accepts both (r,s) and (r,n-s).
finding.source: A valid token; attacker re-encodes its signature segment.
finding.sink: Any application check keyed on the raw token string (replay cache, denylist).

trace.note: base64.urlsafe_b64decode with validate=False drops non-alphabet characters and ignores trailing bits
crypto_segment decoded via base64url_decode
signing_input covers header and payload only, not the signature segment
ECDSA verify accepts high-s signatures, so (r,n-s) also verifies

finding.guards_checked: Cryptographic verification is correct; only the string form is malleable. Count of equivalent HS256 encodings (4) and RS256 (16) comes from base64 arithmetic, not execution. Low severity; depends on the application using token strings as identifiers.

finding.claim: Secure-by-default gaps: HMAC secrets shorter than the digest size are accepted with only a warning (enforce_minimum_key_length defaults to False), and tokens without exp, nbf, or iat pass validation unless the application sets require.
finding.source: Weak HMAC secret (offline brute-force from one captured token); or a signed token omitting exp.
finding.sink: HMAC secret strength; token lifetime enforcement.

effective_options check; warning only when not enforced
HMAC check_key_length returns a message for short keys
require defaults to [] (no mandatory claims)

finding.guards_checked: Warning emitted for short keys; enforcement available as opt-in. Missing exp/nbf/iat is skipped unless require is set. Defaults are a design choice; flagged as low. Verified by reading only.

finding.claim: The HMAC key-type guard rejects PEM and exact-prefix SSH keys but not DER-encoded public keys or SSH keys with leading whitespace, so an asymmetric public key can be used as an HMAC secret when HS* is allowed.
finding.source: Application passes a DER public key, or a whitespace-prefixed ssh- key, with algorithms including HS256/HS384/HS512; attacker signs with that public key as the secret.
finding.sink: HMAC signature verification with the public key bytes as secret (algorithms.py:410-411).
